strengths: Novel gradient-free bi-objective optimization framework for discovering visual invariances that goes beyond predefined transformation families
Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation including representational distance analysis, human classification studies, and observer network testing with proper statistical controls
Evidence that SnS-generated invariants are interpretable and preserve information across different network architectures and processing depths
Interesting empirical finding that robust and standard networks exhibit systematically different invariance patterns
Strong reproducibility practices with released code, detailed hyperparameters, and algorithmic pseudocode provided
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty - essentially applies existing evolutionary optimization (CMA-ES) to a straightforward bi-objective formulation without strong theoretical justification for this particular approach
Unclear practical significance - paper characterizes invariances without providing actionable insights for network design, interpretation, or improvement

Methodological concerns including ambiguous stopping criteria that mix iteration limits with activation thresholds, different initialization strategies between conditions, and narrow focus on single-unit activations
Narrow experimental scope limited to ImageNet-trained CNNs (only 77 readout units tested); no Vision Transformers, other architectures, or modalities; generalization unclear
Insufficient engagement with related work - XDREAM mentioned but not thoroughly compared; limited discussion of alternative invariance discovery methods or theoretical foundations
Small effect sizes in human experiments (differences of 4-5% accuracy) with only 25 participants; underpowered for strong perceptual claims
Weak theoretical grounding - no justification for why this formulation captures meaningful invariances better than alternatives; no ablations on objective design
Biological validity claims are aspirational rather than demonstrated - while claiming relevance to biological vision, no actual neuroscience validation is provided

strengths: Novel gradient-free framework for discovering visual invariances through active search rather than testing predefined transformations—a fundamentally new approach to the problem
Comprehensive experimental methodology with multiple complementary analyses (representational distance, PCA, SVC classification) and proper statistical rigor including multiple comparisons correction

Significant empirical finding that robust networks exhibit more human-interpretable and recognizable invariances, with human subjects study demonstrating robust invariances are significantly more recognizable (p<0.001)
Rigorous characterization of layer-specific invariance structure showing qualitative differences across processing hierarchy (luminance/contrast → texture → pose)
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, hyperparameter specifications, hardware details, open-source code promise, and extensive supplementary material
Well-motivated and clearly presented with effective visualizations that communicate findings from individual examples to aggregated statistics
Relevance beyond computer vision with application to biological visual systems and connections to neuroscience
Thorough controls and baselines including comparisons to XDREAM, natural images, and multiple network variants
weaknesses: Limited architectural scope—only ResNet50 tested; unclear generalizability to Vision Transformers, other CNN architectures, or modern networks
Scalability and computational efficiency not thoroughly analyzed; computational cost grows with network size but no detailed scaling analysis provided
Limited mechanistic understanding of why robust networks develop different invariances; paper documents what exists but provides limited explanation of underlying causes

Interpretation of discovered invariances sometimes unclear; some generated images are quite abstract and the relationship to genuine visual invariances versus optimization artifacts needs deeper discussion
Human experiment with relatively small sample size (N=25) and single perceptual metric (12-AFC); additional metrics and larger participant pool would strengthen claims
Limited exploration of generalization—all findings specific to ImageNet classification; applicability to other vision tasks unexplored
Incomplete comparison to other gradient-free optimization methods and neuroscience-inspired visualization techniques

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple architectures (CNNs, ViTs) with diverse validation approaches (human studies, observer networks, dimensionality analysis)
Principled multi-objective formulation using Pareto optimization to disentangle invariance and adversarial objectives
Interesting empirical finding that L2-robust and standard networks have distinct invariance manifolds at different representation levels
Strong reproducibility: detailed pseudocode, hyperparameters, code availability promised, and explicit ethical review
Multiple validation techniques (PCA, 2NN-ID, human classification, subsampling robustness) strengthen confidence in findings
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating robustness to subsampling and careful experimental design
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core contribution is applying CMA-ES (established 2003 algorithm) with straightforward dual-loss formulation; XDREAM (2019) already used gradient-free methods for similar optimization
Incremental advance over prior work: claimed novelty over XDREAM is overstated; the explicit stretch-squeeze formulation is intuitive but not a significant algorithmic innovation
Small human studies (25 participants) insufficient for strong claims about human perception alignment; many statistical comparisons lack significance testing or multiple-comparison correction
Missing quantitative image quality metrics (FID, IS, LPIPS) and limited baseline comparisons with other feature visualization approaches

Overstated claims: many 'discoveries' are confirmatory (hierarchical feature learning, L2-adversarial robustness effects) rather than novel insights; title promises 'unveiling hidden landscape' but findings are largely incremental
Arbitrary design choices: selection of specific layer indices (low/mid/high level) appears ad-hoc without principled justification; limited ablation on CMA-ES hyperparameters
Restricted scope: analysis limited to object recognition networks; unclear if insights generalize to detection, segmentation, other domains, or visual systems beyond CNNs/ViTs

Methodological concerns: no theoretical justification for Pareto approach vs. weighted-sum optimization; convergence incomplete in some conditions; multiple design choices lack principled justification

strengths: Novel and important research question addressing a fundamental gap in understanding visual invariance—the complete manifold of transformations under which unit activity remains invariant, not just optimal stimuli
Gradient-free, model-agnostic methodology enabling applicability to biological systems and architectures where gradients are inaccessible or ill-defined

Comprehensive and well-executed empirical evaluation including human psychophysics (25 participants across 12 categories), neurophysiology validation, multiple architectures (ResNet, VGG, ViT), and both standard and adversarially robust networks
Rigorous multi-objective optimization using Pareto fronts with CMA-ES, including convergence analysis and ablation studies confirming dual-loss necessity

Compelling empirical findings: invariant images from robust networks are significantly more human-recognizable (~70% vs ~40% accuracy); clear hierarchical patterns; layer-specific effects on interpretability; robustness to subsampling
Valuable insights about adversarial robustness: demonstrates that L2-robustification increases interpretability of high-level invariances but paradoxically decreases it at deeper layers

Methodologically sound with proper statistical testing (Benjamini-Hochberg correction), IRB approval, and excellent reproducibility (code/data available, detailed pseudocode, complete hyperparameters)
Excellent presentation with clear mathematical formulation, high-quality informative figures, and comprehensive supplementary material (10 major sections with extensive analyses)
weaknesses: Limited theoretical depth: primarily empirical work; deeper mechanistic explanation of why robust networks produce more interpretable invariances and analysis of layer-depth effects on interpretability would strengthen contribution

Computational scalability concerns: single optimization requires ~120 seconds; analysis limited to 77 readout units; scaling to large-scale systematic studies unclear; no timing comparisons with related methods like XDREAM

Limited scope of generalization analysis: most experiments on standard architectures (ResNets, VGG, ViT); unclear generalization across different units within same layer; minimal testing on contemporary models (diffusion models, recent foundation models)
Incomplete comparison with closely related work: XDREAM comparison relatively brief; metamers comparison could be deeper; limited ablations testing alternative multi-objective formulations

Sparse biological validation: neurophysiology experiments mentioned but treatment minimal; primary example limited to single unit (candle neuron); claims about applicability to 'biological vision' could be stronger

Incomplete analysis of interesting observations: Page 2 notes invariant images sometimes more pixel-different than affine transformations—paradoxical result deserving deeper investigation; mechanisms of larger pixel distances for invariant vs. adversarial images underexplored

Modest human study sample size: 25 participants with ~50-minute online task; larger sample or in-lab validation would strengthen claims; some convergence runs reach maximum iterations suggesting potential optimization limitations
Limited failure case analysis: when does SnS fail to find meaningful invariances? For which unit types is approach less effective? Hard failure modes not discussed
